summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Ali Beth (1946–1953). He served at Deccan College, Utrecht University, and the University of Chicago (1957–1964).

J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from around 1982 to 2002 and held an attested affiliation with SOAS University of London in 1996.

J. C. Wright is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who served as a professor at the University of London. He earned an MD at the University of London in 2007 and was a specialist gynaecologist at Hamlin Fistula International in 2013.

J. Duncan M. Derrett was an Indologist who studied at Emanuel School, Jesus College, Oxford (~1940–1947), and SOAS University of London (~1947–1949). He held a post at the University of London from around 1949 to 1982.

J. F. Blakiston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Wellington College. He spent his career at the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as assistant (1911), Superintendent (1916), and Director-General (1935–1937).

J. G. Jennings was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an M.A. at the University of Oxford (~1885–1889). He served as teacher and Principal at Muir Central College (1898–1913) and Director of Public Instruction for Bihar and Orissa (~1917–1921).

J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar who studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University (Ph.D. ~1975). He founded ISAR (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. H. F. Hamilton was an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford from around 1877 to 1881. In 1879, he served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service.

J. J. Johnson was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and Durham University (M.A. 1903). He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from around 1879 to 1917.

J. L. Shaw is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied under Bimal Krishna Matilal and completed studies at Rice University (~1969–1973). He held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington from approximately 1973 to 2014.
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from around 1897 to 1923.

J. N. Farquhar was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Aberdeen, Christ Church, and Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He later served as the Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Manchester (1927–1929).

J. N. Reuter was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Helsinki, Jena, and Berlin under Otto Donner, Berthold Delbrück, and Albrecht Weber. He served as Acting Professor at the University of Helsinki from 1891 to 1931.

J. Nelson Fraser was an Indologist who served as Professor of English Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1896–1906) and as Principal of the Secondary Training College, Bombay (~1906–1918).

id: P:J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong
summary: J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong was a linguist who completed his studies at Leiden University from around 1905 to 1913. He later held academic appointments at Leiden University in 1922 and from 1935 to 1956.

J. P. Mallory is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Occidental, UCLA, UC Merced, and UC Irvine, he served as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011).

J. P. Mills worked in Indology and related fields. He was educated at Windlesham House School, Winchester College, and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1909–1912), and later served as a Reader at SOAS University of London (1948–1955).
J. Peter L. Gwynn was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education at St Columba's College (~1929–1935), Trinity College, Hartford (B.A. ~1935–1938), and University College London.

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, with teachers including Alfred North Whitehead and Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. S. Negi is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He was engaged in research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1977 and served as Chief Editor at CIHTS (attested 1993–2001).
